newsitem.title: USA: Dlr mixed in extremely light trade at U.S. close.
newsitem.headline: Dlr mixed in extremely light trade at U.S. close.

text.p: *Dlr/mark ends off highs in U.S., mark fell prey to stg, lira, and yen strength. Dlr/yen closes at lower level, trade light.

*Mark hurt by Buba Meister's remark German tax estimate shows EMU qualification "thorny" for Bonn too. *All eyes on Tuesday FOMC meeting, new Reuters poll shows 21 of 39 primary dealers calling for steady policy. *Japan April trade surplus jumps.
The dollar ended mixed in quiet trade on Monday, propelled higher against the mark which suffered a beating on the European crosses but quashed once again versus a resilient yen, dealers said.
The mark succumbed to strong buying in sterling and lira while the yen resumed a rally sparked overnight after news Japan's international trade surplus jumped in April.
The dollar rose to 1.7075/85 marks by the end of trade on Monday from 1.7032/37 at the open, but closed lower at 115.57/67 yen from 116.25/30.
"The dollar was helped by two things -- mark selling against the crosses and stop-loss buy orders above 1.7080/90 marks that got triggered," said a New York currency trader.

Trade was slow as most European bourses were closed due to the Pentecost holiday, allowing market attention to fixate on the probability of U.S. central bankers raising official interest rates on Tuesday in an attempt to preempt inflation.

Fed officials hiked rates for the first time in more than two years on March 25, but Wall Street remains divided on whether a second such move is necessary given signs of an economic slowdown in recent April data releases.

A Reuters poll published on Monday showed that 21 of 39 primary dealers -- large banks which act as an intermediary between the Treasury Department and government markets -- expect rates to remain unchanged.

"Tomorrow's meeting is the big focus of the market. The consensus is fairly even at about 50/50 as to whether the Fed will do anything," said Dennis Pettit, foreign exchange manager at Long Term Credit Bank of Japan in New York.
"My thoughts are perhaps there's not sufficient political cover for them to raise rates tomorrow and that they might defer until July," Pettit added.
Remarks from Bundesbank board Member Edgar Meister exacerbated mark weakness against the British pound, lira and yen, thus aiding the dollar, dealers said.

Meister sparked concern that criteria for membership in Europe's planned single currency may be relaxed, which in turn would enable more countries to qualify and possibly weaken the resulting single currency.

Meister said Germany's recent efforts to recover an 18 billion mark tax revenue shortfall to meet qualifications shows how "thorny" meeting the single-currency criteria is for Germany as well as most other European nations.

"It's not really a strong dollar, but a depreciating mark and appreciating pound against the mark, which has propelled the dollar higher against the mark," said John Nelson, foreign exchange trading manager at ABN-AMRO Bank.

The lira gained against the mark on expectations of an interest rate cut in the near future as the Bank of Italy lowered its repurchase rate on Monday to a historic low of 6.78 percent. Sterling was buoyed by better-than-expected UK public sector debt data.
The dollar dipped to a session low of 114.85 yen after Japan's Finance Ministry reported its customs-cleared trade surplus more than doubled in April from a year earlier to 831.48 billion yen.
The trade surplus with the United States, often a source of friction, surged 174.1 percent in April from a year earlier to 468.97 billion yen.

In other trading, the dollar rose to 1.4270/80 Swiss francs from 1.4225/35 and fell to Canadian $1.3713/18 from C$1.3727/32. Sterling rose to $1.6390/00 from $1.6385/90. The Australian dollar closed at $0.7742/47 from $0.7725/30.
((-- Roanne Daniels, 212-859-1677))
